articles.description: One of the Iranian tankers struck was near a key area in Iran's oil-export system, according to U.S. Central Command.
articles.title: U.S. strikes Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for missile attacks on Navy ships

articles.author: Ali Asif Shawon
articles.description: It was a light bulb moment: If monsoon rains keep kids from safely getting to school, let's create a floating school to pick them up! Bangladesh pioneered the idea. How's it doing?
articles.title: Whatever happened to the floating schools of Bangladesh?

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow to revive efforts to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called for a halt to air attacks during their visit, but Moscow has not publicly responded.
articles.title: U.S. envoys in Moscow in new push for peace between Russia and Ukraine

articles.author: Linda Holmes
articles.description: NPR's Linda Holmes is a daily puzzle devotee. She recommends games that will test your knowledge of geography, history, and even the most obscure corners of Wikipedia.
articles.title: If you prefer puzzles to doomscrolling, here are 5 great games to check out

articles.author: Barrie Hardymon
articles.description: Ann M. Martin's beloved series has influenced generations of readers. We're still asking: Which babysitter are you?
articles.title: 40 years later, 'The Baby-Sitters Club' is still helping readers see themselves

articles.author: Maham Javaid
articles.description: Democrats and Republicans have found common ground in this campaign season. Both parties have poured millions into ads attacking data centers as the public continues to protest the AI facilities.
articles.title: Voters are fed up with data centers. Both parties are trying to cash in for midterms

articles.author: Meg Anderson
articles.description: As political races heat up heading into the midterms, candidates from both parties are increasingly joining the fray to voice concerns over Flock surveillance cameras.
articles.title: Flock cameras draw opposition from across the political spectrum

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte has posted bail after order issued for her arrest on charges she publicly threatened to arrange assassination of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and two others.
articles.title: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte posts bail after arrest

articles.author: Jewel Bright
articles.description: The U.N. has backed a new map showing Africa in its true relative size, with the U.S. standing alone in opposition.
articles.title: The U.N. backs a new world map showing Africa in its true relative size

articles.author: Andrea Hsu
articles.description: A report from Labor Department investigators found former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer violated her own department's policy prohibiting harassment. She resigned in April.
articles.title: 4 things investigators learned about the dysfunction at Trump's Labor Department

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv
articles.description:
Serhii Beskrestnov says deadlock on frontline and increasing use of deep strikes is placing civilians and infrastructure at greater risk
Russia and Ukraine are locked in an escalating war of long-range strikes with a growing risk to civilians in which neither side can entirely prevail, according to Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s defence technology adviser.
Serhii Beskrestnov, widely known by his call sign, Flash, said he was worried about the prospects for Kyiv this winter, and suggested elderly people should be evacuated in case Russian bombing were to knock out the capital’s energy supply.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Nobody will win’: Zelenskyy adviser warns of mutual destruction if war with Russia continues

articles.author: Tory Shepherd
articles.description:
Follow today’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Duniam targets ‘frivolous’ asylum seeker claims
The opposition is “very close” to “having a full migration package”, Duniam says. He says they’re willing to work with the government and that illegal overstayers must be deported.
We spend more per student per year than we ever have before and we’ve got declining standards across the board, and the problem with the curriculum is we have left foundations behind.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: up to 6,000 tradies to get free qualifications under Labor scheme

articles.author: William Christou and agencies
articles.description:
‘Substantive plans’ will be announced in ‘coming weeks’ as envoys head to Kyiv for talks with Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy
Donald Trump’s envoys “discussed substantive plans for next steps” for ending the war between Ukraine and Russia during their meeting on Saturday in Moscow with Vladimir Putin, the White House said.
Those steps would be announced in “coming weeks”, a White House official said in a statement, and the envoys “look forward to equally productive meetings tomorrow [Sunday] in Ukraine”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump envoys and Putin discussed ‘next steps’ for ending Ukraine war, White House says

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
Anika Wells expected to release legislation creating a digital duty of care in parliament this week, but Coalition argues it is ‘attempt to censor the internet’

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here

Labor’s plan to crack down on social media algorithms faces significant opposition in federal parliament, with the opposition leader, Angus Taylor, warning against efforts by the government to “censor” free speech online.
The communications minister, Anika Wells, is expected to release draft legislation creating a digital duty of care for social media users in Australia as parliament returns this week.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labor plans crackdown on social media algorithms as Taylor says he’s ‘deeply sceptical’

articles.author: Andrew Messenger
articles.description:
Police search for alleged attacker, in his 50s, after incident in Gippsland town of Tyers

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Three people have been taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries after an alleged axe attack in Victoria, with police still searching for the suspect.
The alleged attacker, who is known to the victims, came to an address in the Gippsland town of Tyers at about 12.30pm on Saturday, according to a spokesperson for Victoria police.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Manhunt after alleged axe attack in Victoria leaves three people with serious injuries

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Preservationists worry board may seize on incident ‘to make the point that the whole thing needs to be shut down’
Falling debris from a ceiling in the grand foyer of the John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts may have complicated a battle over renovations of the Washington DC arts center that could result in the building being demolished.
A portion of the ceiling collapsed on Friday evening after heavy rain swept through the area, prompting officials to temporarily close the Edward Durell Stone-designed building. No one was injured by the debris.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Falling ceiling debris at Kennedy Center may mire debate over renovations

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
US president suggests he might support his Argentinian ally’s drive to reclaim sovereignty of disputed islands
Donald Trump has long embraced vengeance. “I am your retribution,” he declared to an admiring audience at the 2023 Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) as he commenced his march back to the White House.
It is unlikely Argentina, and far-flung holdovers of the former British empire, were on the US president’s mind at the time.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s pique with UK could lead to favor to acolyte Milei over Falklands

articles.author: Angus Thomson and agency
articles.description:
Blaze causes electricity supply failure and disruption of services to airport and Reading
Hundreds of passengers were evacuated from a train, and services to Heathrow airport were cancelled, after a fire near tracks in the London Paddington area caused major disruptions to London’s rail network.
The fire caused an electricity supply failure which left all lines between Paddington and the airport blocked, National Rail said on Saturday afternoon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: London Paddington fire causes rail chaos as Heathrow trains cancelled

articles.author: Associated Press in Bogotá
articles.description:
Officials accuse National Liberation Army of launching strike followed by clash inside military compound
An attack involving explosives dropped from drones followed by a clash inside a military compound in north-eastern Colombia has killed at least three soldiers and wounded four, Colombia’s army said on Saturday.
Local authorities blamed the attack – which took place late on Friday – on the rebel National Liberation Army (ELN).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Drone attack blamed on guerrillas kills at least three soldiers in Colombia

articles.author: Press Association
articles.description:
Duty falls by precedent to William to attend service of late monarch, alongside Princess Royal, who is godmother to new king Haakon VIII 
The Prince of Wales is to represent his father at the funeral of King Harald V of Norway next week, Buckingham Palace has announced.
William, the heir to the throne, will be joined by his aunt the Princess Royal, who is attending in a private and personal capacity as godmother of the new king, Haakon VIII.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prince William to represent King Charles at funeral of Norway’s King Harald V

articles.author: Roque Planas
articles.description:
Latest data from Gallup, showing 49% leaning Democrat and 39% Republican, marks sharp reversal from 2024
More voters are identifying as Democrats and shying away from calling themselves Republican, according to the latest quarterly data published by Gallup.
Some 49% of voters surveyed leaned Democrat, including independent voters asked to pick one party or the other. Only 39% of respondents leaned Republican.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More voters identifying as Democrats and not calling themselves Republican

articles.author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
articles.description:
Sector has avoided issue because of stigma fears, expert warns ahead of closure of Nottingham attacks inquiry 
Mental health organisations have “failed to acknowledge” the risk of violence from a minority of people with severe mental illnesses, the chief executive of Mind has said ahead of the closure of the inquiry into the Nottingham attacks.
Dr Sarah Hughes, who has led mental health charity Mind for four years and has worked in the sector for almost four decades, said charities had shied away from addressing the risk of violence due to the fact it had increased the stigma and harassment around people with mental health conditions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mental health groups have ‘failed to acknowledge’ risk of violence, says Mind chief

articles.author: Benita Kolovos and Henry Belot
articles.description:
A machete-wielding robber, a ‘tsunami of debt’ … campaigns echoing opposition talking points outspend major parties

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man clad in a balaclava and brandishing a machete terrorises a worker at a petrol station before firebombing the building on the way out.
A woman gives birth on the side of the road, unable to reach a hospital due to ambulance ramping and crater-like potholes, which also stop a fire truck in its tracks.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alarming AI ads are flooding social media in the lead-up to Victoria’s election. But who is behind them?

articles.author: Donna Ferguson, Priya Bharadia and agencies
articles.description:
Port authorities say access roads ‘free flowing’ again after large group forces road closures in both directions 
Dozens of people dressed in black and wearing balaclavas blocked the road at the port of Dover in Kent, forcing closures in both directions on Saturday morning.
Kent police said they were were in attendance and engaging with the protest, which the Port of Dover described as a “public order incident”. No arrests were made during the incident. Responsibility for the demonstration appears to have been claimed by an anti-immigration group with links to the far right.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Black-clad protesters in balaclavas block road at port of Dover in Kent

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Leading second-wave feminist co-founded Women’s Media Center with Jane Fonda and Gloria Steinem
Robin Morgan, a child star of the 1940s and 50s who grew up to become an all-American radical as a poet, essayist, editor and second-wave feminist, has died. She was 85.
Morgan’s death was confirmed Saturday by the Women’s Media Center, an organization she co-founded with Jane Fonda and the celebrated author and activist Gloria Steinem, who died Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Robin Morgan, child star who became feminist, poet and editor, dies aged 85

articles.author: AFP in Cairo
articles.description:
Sarah Khalifa, 39, charged with forming organised criminal gang to manufacture and traffic drugs
An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drug case, official media reported on Saturday.
The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her programme Mission Impossible, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Egyptian TV presenter among 12 sentenced to death for drug crime

articles.author: Taz Ali (now) and Hamish Mackay (earlier)
articles.description:
‘Sometimes we will get things wrong and get a bit of a kicking for it,’ party leader tells gathering in Birmingham 
No real mention by Anderson of the problems that overshadowed events yesterday. He ended his opening speech saying: "Yesterday was great. Today is going to be absolutely brilliant.”
Laila Cunningham is speaking next.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Farage brushes aside Reform controversies in closing conference speech – UK politics as it happened

articles.author: Ben Quinn and Peter Walker
articles.description:
Reform UK leader maintains innocence in overseas funding controversy on last day of party conference
Nigel Farage has claimed that he “wasn’t even listening” during a meeting at the centre of a controversy about whether his party considered evading the law on accepting donations from overseas.
The Reform UK leader also claimed he knew donation law “better than anybody” during interviews as he sought to salvage the final day of his party conference from the fallout that has already cost him two of his closest aides.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I wasn’t even listening,’ Farage says of donations scandal meeting

articles.author: Marina Dunbar and agencies
articles.description:
Officials said US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided attacks before three Iranian tankers were struck by the US
The US military said Saturday it struck three Iranian oil tankers after US navy warships came under missile attack, further escalating tensions in the region and warning it would “if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet”.
According to the military, a US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided “multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks” while patrolling the region. No US personnel were injured.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US military says it struck three Iranian tankers after American warships came under missile attack

articles.author: Thor Benson
articles.description:
Politicians on the right and left are pushing back against Flock as more Americans voice opposition to the tech
Growing factions from both sides of the political aisle in the US are pushing back against surveillance cameras made by a single company, a rare response in a sharply divided country with a president pushing an unwaveringly pro-tech agenda.
The bipartisan backlash against Flock Safety cameras resembles nationwide rage toward the construction of large datacenters that power artificial intelligence. Polling shows roughly 75% of Americans oppose new datacenter construction in their areas.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cut the cameras: Flock surveillance cameras spur rare bipartisan backlash

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Houthi rebel offensive against government forces on west coast leads to some of deadliest clashes in years
Clashes between Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthi rebel movement have killed more than 60 people, including civilians, as the Houthis pushed forward with a military offensive on Yemen’s western coast.
Twenty-six government troops and 31 Houthi fighters were killed during several hours of fighting in the country’s south-west on Saturday, medical and military sources told Agence France-Presse (AFP). A missile strike also killed six civilians and injured seven others travelling by bus in the city of Taiz.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Civilians among at least 60 killed in Yemen as ground fighting escalates

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
District attorney must decide whether to retry case after jury’s failure to reach verdict despite hours of deliberation
Lindsay Clancy, prosecutors, defense lawyers, the judge and millions watching on are back where they started after her five-week trial over the murder of her three children ended in a mistrial.
America’s saddest case has ceased for the moment, but the legal wrangling is not over, and a second trial could now be on the horizon, prolonging and repeating an agonizing spectacle that has gripped America and the world.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial ends in dramatic deadlock – what comes next?

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Chinese man at Trishuli hydropower project and Nepali woman in Nuwakot found 10 days into rescue operation
Emergency responders have rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal.
The Nepali military said on Saturday a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flash flood disaster

articles.author: Matan Cohen in Jerusalem, and Julian Borger
articles.description:
Exclusive: Guardian investigation reveals targeting of World Central Kitchen convoy was result of widely used military tactic

Death on the road to Rafah: the night the IDF targeted WCK aid workers

Seven aid workers killed in an airstrike in Gaza were marked as targets under an Israeli military practice of establishing guilt by association, a Guardian investigation shows.
A top Israeli military prosecutor announced last month that he would not pursue criminal proceedings for the April 2024 incident in which drones fired missiles at three clearly marked World Central Kitchen (WCK) cars soon after they had escorted a food aid delivery to Gaza. Three British humanitarian workers along with an Australian, a Palestinian, a Pole and a dual US-Canadian national were killed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Guilt by association’: why seven international aid workers were killed in Israeli airstrike

articles.author: Patrick Wintour in Rome
articles.description:
Security experts fear Putin may be winning hybrid war with the west amid rise of pro-Kremlin, far-right parties
Defence planners working with Nato fear that if war broke out with Russia, Europe could not currently sustain a prolonged war of attrition owing to a public lack of war readiness, a conference on the future of European military coordination heard this week.
The pessimism reflects concern that Russia may be winning a so-called hybrid war with Europe, weakening the options available to Nato war planners in the event of military conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Europe would not be able to sustain war of attrition with Russia, defence officials say

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Carlos de Almeida Baptista Júnior describes 2022 meeting in new book as ex-leader’s son vies with Lula for presidency
The far-right populist Jair Bolsonaro was in his final days as Brazil’s president when, six weeks after losing the election and still refusing to recognise the result, he summoned the heads of the armed forces to a meeting.
The defence minister, Gen Paulo Sérgio Nogueira de Oliveira, took out a document from a plastic folder and handed copies to the commanders of the navy, army and air force.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It cost me many friendships’: former Brazil military chief reveals inside struggle to stop Bolsonaro’s coup

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Anwar, who lives in Glasgow, says Home Office refused visa application despite Maryam having cancer
A man living in the UK has said he believes his sister-in-law who died from cancer in Gaza would still be alive today if the Home Office had agreed to bring her and her family to Britain.
Anwar, who lives in Glasgow, fled Gaza in 2020 and was granted refugee status in the UK in 2021. After the destruction of large areas of Gaza by Israeli forces following the Hamas attacks on Israel in October 2023, he applied to bring his brother Hassan, Hassan’s wife, Maryam, their two young children and other family members to the UK in October 2025. He said the Home Office rejected their application.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gaza refugee says sister-in-law ‘would be alive’ if Home Office had let her come to UK

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Scale of deportations made public for first time amid criticism of hardline approach to UK citizens
Sweden has confirmed 458 British citizens have been deported or forcibly removed by police since Brexit.
It is the first time the scale of the deportations of citizens who failed to secure residency in Sweden post-Brexit has been made public and comes amid mounting criticism of a cruel and hardline approach to Britons who had chosen to make the country their home before Brexit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sweden confirms 458 Britons deported or forcibly removed since Brexit

articles.author: Australian Associated Press with Guardian staff
articles.description:
A total fire ban is in place for greater Sydney with extreme fire danger exacerbated by hot and windy conditions

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Summer heat is due to arrive early across much of eastern Australia with potentially record early September temperatures predicted for Brisbane and Sydney, while snow was expected in southern New South Wales.
Maximum temperatures in Sydney during the first days of September were on track to match the city’s midsummer average of 26.4C, warmer than any other start to spring since the city’s Observatory Hill station opened in 1858.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sydney reaches 33C in potentially warmest start to spring since mid-1800s, while snow forecast in southern NSW

articles.author: Julian Borger and Matan Cohen in Jerusalem
articles.description:
The Israeli army had helped plan the delivery of food aid on 1 April 2024, but things went wrong from the beginning and ended in seven deaths
• Exclusive: why seven international aid workers were killed in Israeli airstrike
On the evening of 1 April 2024, a team of aid workers from World Central Kitchen (WCK) stood on Gaza’s Mediterranean shore overseeing the unloading of a barge full of desperately needed food on a makeshift jetty made of sand and rubble.
The Gaza war had been raging for six months and Israel’s closure of land crossings had left the whole territory facing the threat of famine. WCK and local Palestinian contractors had constructed the jetty out of everything they could lay their hands on, including debris from the bombed house of one of the contractors, so that the pallets of humanitarian assistance could be delivered by boat from Cyprus.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Death on the road to Rafah: the night the IDF targeted World Central Kitchen aid workers

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
articles.description:
Togo-sponsored resolution called to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland
The United Nations has voted to adopt a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size.
In a session at its headquarters in New York, the UN general assembly officially retired the 16th-century Mercator projection in favour of one based on the more accurate 2018 Equal Earth design.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UN votes to adopt new world map that shows Africa’s true scale

articles.author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Abelardo De La Espriella posts video of himself with rows of body bags as performative populism continues to sweep Americas
Colombia’s hardline president, Abelardo De La Espriella, has provoked outrage after posting a video on social media in which he strides through rows of white body bags that he says contained the corpses of 23 “neutralised” guerrillas.
De La Espriella took power last month vowing “all-out war” against illegal armed groups and he published the footage on Thursday in an apparent attempt to show he was fulfilling that pledge.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Colombia president provokes disgust by posing with bodies of ‘terrorists’

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu
articles.description:
Officials say pair were rescued from Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel in Nepal after being trapped at depth of 170 metres
Two people have been pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal nine days after deadly flash floods buried the projects in deep mud and left them trapped.
The workers were rescued during an operation at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, a hydropower project in one of the areas worst affected by last week’s floods, according to the army spokesperson Brig Gen Raja Ram Basnet.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two workers pulled alive from tunnel nine days after Nepal-Tibet floods

articles.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
articles.description:
President cites Trump’s suggestion that he might reconsider US stance on British sovereignty and threatens swifter sanctions on UK oil interests
President Javier Milei has said “winds of change” favourable to Argentina’s claim to the Falkland Islands are blowing around the world in a televised address, citing signs that Donald Trump may reconsider the US position on the islands’ sovereignty.
“Recently, President Trump declared that the US is re-evaluating its historic position in relation to the Malvinas,” he said, using the Argentinian name for the islands.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Javier Milei: ‘winds of change’ support Argentina’s claim to Falkland Islands

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
Seoul reportedly seeking parliamentary approval to send military assets to Middle East but president’s office plays down claims
South Korea is reviewing a possible deployment of military assets to the strait of Hormuz amid pressure from Donald Trump over Seoul’s reluctance to provide support in the region, according to domestic media reports.
Citing unnamed government and military sources, the reports published on Thursday and Friday said preparations were under way and that the government intended to seek parliamentary approval for a new deployment. The reports, which appeared in major South Korean outlets, said the exact scale and timing had not been agreed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South Korea pushes back on reports it is readying Hormuz deployment amid US pressure

articles.author: Heather Stewart and Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
Jump lifts currency to highest level against dollar in a month, while global markets remain jittery

Business live – latest updates

The Japanese yen has soared by more than 2% against the dollar amid speculation the Bank of Japan is set to raise interest rates.
The latest jump on Thursday lifted the yen to its highest level against the dollar in a month, at 155.57, and followed a 0.9% move the previous day.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Yen soars as Bank of Japan tipped to raise interest rates

articles.author: Stephen Burgen in Barcelona
articles.description:
Pedro Sánchez continues to defend Rabat after police report claiming border forces helped 70,000 cross border

Europe live – latest updates

Spain has seen no evidence “whatsoever” that Morocco planned or facilitated a mass border breach into its north African territory of Ceuta, the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has told parliament.
The address on Thursday followed the emergence of a police report, commissioned by a judge and widely quoted in the media, claiming Moroccan border forces had actively aided about 70,000 people to cross the border in late July.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Spain’s PM says no evidence ‘whatsoever’ Morocco behind Ceuta border breach

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu
articles.description:
About 46 people believed to be trapped in ‘room-like’ structure inside hydro plant tunnel on Nepal-Tibet border

After the flood: human suffering on an unfathomable scale in Nepal’s worst-hit districts

Nepal authorities have said they are “confident” that dozens of workers in Nepal’s Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant are still alive, more than a week after deadly flash floods left them trapped in an underground chamber.
Authorities said that at least 639 workers were still missing from hydropower plants built along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Triushuli rivers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Dozens of trapped hydropower tunnel workers in Nepal could still be alive, official says

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Sharpeville
articles.description:
Claim relating to 1960 attack on hundreds of protesters part of wave of litigation over apartheid crimes in South Africa
The day dawned brightly on 21 March 1960, as residents of the South African township of Sharpeville gathered to protest against pass laws, which forced “Black, Indian and Coloured” South Africans to carry documents at all times specifying where they were allowed to be.
Abraham Mofokeng joined the march, one of dozens organised nationwide by the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC), a breakaway group from the African National Congress (ANC). “The weather was very nice, the sun was out. You could not have suspected that the day would go so horribly,” said Mofokeng, who was then a 20-year-old factory worker.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We continue to suffer’: victims of apartheid-era Sharpeville massacre demand compensation

articles.author: Jonathan Watts
articles.description:
Oil consumption plummets and EV sales soar as analysts say demand may not fully return even if crude price falls
China’s carbon dioxide emissions fell by 1% after the outbreak of the US-Israeli war on Iran, thanks to a sharp reduction in oil consumption and a steady rise in the use of electric vehicles and public transport, analysis shows.
The report reveals the role of clean energy in cushioning the price shocks caused by the strait of Hormuz crisis to the world’s biggest oil importer. It also reinforces hopes that China, which is the world’s biggest greenhouse gas emitter, may be nearing a turning point in decarbonising its economy.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: China’s falling emissions amid Iran war spark hope of decarbonisation watershed

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Bangladeshi complainants allege Rampal power station’s pollution and climate risks threaten the Sunderbans, a world heritage site
Barclays Bank is facing a formal complaint over its financial links to a coal-fired power station near the Sundarbans, the world’s largest mangrove forest and home to millions of people in Bangladesh and India.
Three complainants from the region have submitted a case to the UK government’s Office for Responsible Business Conduct, alleging that the British bank breached international guidelines by underwriting companies involved in the emission-heavy Maitree super thermal power project, also known as the Rampal power plant.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Barclays faces complaint over backing for power plant near world’s largest mangrove forest

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
articles.description:
Referendum result means fewer seats in parliament and new rules on candidates, ahead of December elections
Guinea-Bissau voters have approved a new constitution, which critics say will undermine democracy, that significantly expands presidential powers ahead of elections due in December.
According to provisional results, 70% of voters approved sweeping changes in the tiny west African state’s first constitutional amendment since revisions that ended the one-party socialist state more than three decades ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New constitution in Guinea-Bissau will undermine democracy, opponents say

articles.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
articles.description:
Speed limit dropped from 60km/h for around 70% of general roads in the hope of making narrow streets of crowded cities safer
Drivers on residential roads in Japan have been forced to take their foot off the accelerator, after the speed limit was slashed from 60km/h (37mph) to 30km/h in an attempt to reduce deaths and injuries among pedestrians on narrow urban streets.
The new limit, which went into effect on Tuesday, applies to residential roads with no centre line or maximum speed signs, media reports said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japan halves speed limit to 30km/h on all narrow city streets

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Several missing Australians have been found since Tuesday morning, bringing the total citizens unaccounted for to 38

Australians missing in the Nepal floods: what we know so far

A total of five Australians missing after devastating floods ravaged the Nepal-Tibet border last week have been found.
Of the five Australians confirmed safe, one was found in Nepal, one in Tibet, and three outside the crisis-hit area. The total number still missing is 38.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Relief as five Australians missing in Nepal-Tibet flood disaster found alive

articles.author: Angus Thomson
articles.description:
More than 1,000 people confirmed dead and more than 4,000, including 36 British nationals, remain missing
A British aid worker was mistakenly identified by Nepalese authorities as a rescued survivor after returning to Kathmandu on a humanitarian aid flight.
Alastair Chambers, a 45-year-old former Gloucester councillor, said he flew to Nepal last week to distribute sleeping bags, food and essentials to communities cut off by collapsed bridges.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British aid worker mistakenly identified as a survivor of Nepal-Tibet disaster

articles.author: William Christou and agencies
articles.description:
‘Substantive plans’ will be announced in ‘coming weeks’ as envoys head to Kyiv for talks with Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy
Donald Trump’s envoys “discussed substantive plans for next steps” for ending the war between Ukraine and Russia during their meeting on Saturday in Moscow with Vladimir Putin, the White House said.
Those steps would be announced in “coming weeks”, a White House official said in a statement, and the envoys “look forward to equally productive meetings tomorrow [Sunday] in Ukraine”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump envoys and Putin discussed ‘next steps’ for ending Ukraine war, White House says

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Preservationists worry board may seize on incident ‘to make the point that the whole thing needs to be shut down’
Falling debris from a ceiling in the grand foyer of the John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts may have complicated a battle over renovations of the Washington DC arts center that could result in the building being demolished.
A portion of the ceiling collapsed on Friday evening after heavy rain swept through the area, prompting officials to temporarily close the Edward Durell Stone-designed building. No one was injured by the debris.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Falling ceiling debris at Kennedy Center may mire debate over renovations

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
US president suggests he might support his Argentinian ally’s drive to reclaim sovereignty of disputed islands
Donald Trump has long embraced vengeance. “I am your retribution,” he declared to an admiring audience at the 2023 Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) as he commenced his march back to the White House.
It is unlikely Argentina, and far-flung holdovers of the former British empire, were on the US president’s mind at the time.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s pique with UK could lead to favor to acolyte Milei over Falklands

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Judge issues order as part of discovery process in lawsuit brought by non-profit into now defunct compensation fund
A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to reveal who set up the structure of a controversial $1.8bn “anti-weaponization fund” to recompense victims of so-called political lawfare that was reportedly dropped by the justice department last month.
Ivan Davis, the US magistrate judge for the eastern district of Virginia, issued the order compelling discovery materials from the government as part of a lawsuit brought by the Democracy Forward non-profit on behalf of plaintiffs including a fired prosecutor and a college professor acquitted of assaulting federal agents at a protest against an immigration raid in California.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Judge orders Trump administration to reveal who set up $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponization fund’

articles.author: Thor Benson
articles.description:
Politicians on the right and left are pushing back against Flock as more Americans voice opposition to the tech
Growing factions from both sides of the political aisle in the US are pushing back against surveillance cameras made by a single company, a rare response in a sharply divided country with a president pushing an unwaveringly pro-tech agenda.
The bipartisan backlash against Flock Safety cameras resembles nationwide rage toward the construction of large datacenters that power artificial intelligence. Polling shows roughly 75% of Americans oppose new datacenter construction in their areas.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cut the cameras: Flock surveillance cameras spur rare bipartisan backlash

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Todd Blanche’s remarks are part of a totally-not-invented moral panic that stretches the limits of the imagination
Being a public school teacher in the US these days is tough. You’ve got to pay for a lot of your own supplies, deal with smartphone-addicted children and perform gender-affirming surgeries on your lunch break.
Luckily our intrepid attorney general, Todd Blanche, is on the case. Blanche appeared on Fox News this week to decry a “pandemic” of gender transitions in schools across the US. “There’s not a parent in America, no matter where you live, that would want their school to change and call their child by a different name and not expect to be told about that. We partnered with the Department of Education recently to combat this very trend and, really, pandemic that’s happening in some school districts around the country,” Blanche said. He seemed more concerned with name changes than with surgery, but the president himself has suggested on several occasions that schools are furtively doing surgery on children. During a campaign speech in 2024, for example, Donald Trump said: “Can you imagine … your son leaves the house and you say: ‘Jimmy, I love you so much. Go have a good day in school,’ and your son comes back with a brutal operation? Can you even imagine this?”
Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The US attorney general is fretting about a ‘pandemic’ of gender transitions in schools | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Jonathan Freedland
articles.description:
Such is the US president’s narcissism that he would see a Democratic victory as proof that he’s indispensable – meanwhile, his every decision spells calamity for voters
What is Donald Trump playing at? If it’s true that the best way of understanding the behaviour of an organisation is to assume it’s controlled by a secret cabal of its enemies, perhaps that same logic extends to the current conduct of the president of the United States. Maybe he secretly wants Republicans to lose the looming midterm elections that will decide the balance of power in the US for the next two years and for which the first postal ballots were sent out today.
That’s not as mad a theory as it sounds. Indeed, there are at least two reasons why Trump might either be unbothered by Republican defeat in November or even covertly desire it. We’ll come to those, but let’s start with a pattern of behaviour that is hard to explain as anything other than calculated self-sabotage.
Jonathan Freedland is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How much does Donald Trump care about winning the midterms? Apparently, not much at all | Jonathan Freedland

articles.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
articles.description:
Believed to be first US deportations to fourth country, six face ‘horrific conditions’ in Equatorial Guinea, say lawyers
In late August, around 20 people were put on a flight in the US, shackled at the wrists, waist and ankles, and sent to Liberia as part of one of the largest third-country deportation arrangements of Donald Trump’s second term.
Although more than 23,000 people have been sent to 26 countries other than their own since last year, that day saw something that had not happened before: six people refused to get off the plane – and were instead taken to another country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Six people refused to get off ICE deportation plane – now they’re held in limbo in Equatorial Guinea

articles.author: Joanna Walters in New York
articles.description:
Letty Cottin Pogrebin says Steinem taught the younger feminist how to change a ‘man’s world’ not adjust to it

Gloria Steinem, groundbreaking feminist campaigner, dies aged 92

‘We badly need to raise our boys more like our girls’: Gloria Steinem – a life in quotes

When an up and coming feminist author and journalist bumped into Gloria Steinem at a women’s conference in Washington DC in 1971 she was awed but also realized she had been on the wrong track by “asking women to adjust” to “a man’s world” rather than organizing to change it, as the more senior activist of the two was doing.
Letty Cottin Pogrebin and Steinem ended up comparing notes and brainstorming until the wee hours of the following morning and Steinem asked her to come on board with a project she was cooking up – Ms magazine.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Founding editor of Ms magazine on Gloria Steinem: ‘The least egomaniacal person’

articles.author: Steven Greenhouse
articles.description:
The trillions in tax cuts going to the rich and corporations could have instead been used to address the affordability crisis
Dear reader, I recognize that your eyes might glaze over at any mention of the nation’s $40tn federal debt. But your reaction to this mind-boggling number shouldn’t be ennui; it should be outrage and dismay.
Outrage is in order because the nation’s debt has climbed to more than $40tn under Donald Trump, even though back in 2016, when the debt was less than half what it is today, candidate Trump insisted that he’d totally eliminate the debt within eight years. That was yet another example of the Demagogue-in-Chief’s willingness to say anything, no matter how insincere or untrue, to woo voters.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: In 2016, Trump pledged to erase the federal debt. It just hit $40tn | Steven Greenhouse

articles.author: Jason Wilson
articles.description:
Marx’s All Things Possible Florida model uses private funds for cop pay and surveillance tools without public oversight
The All Things Possible ministry (ATP) is an unusual, and critics say potentially dangerous, operation. It has in the last year funded surveillance equipment and salaries for out-of-state law enforcement agencies, hired a range of private security and intelligence contractors, and is connected to a network of other self-appointed sex-trafficking rescue groups whose leading figures have attracted significant controversy.
And its founder is the man who wants to be Colorado’s next governor.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Colorado’s Republican governor nominee linked to controversial anti-sex-trafficking ministry

articles.author: Luke Harding
articles.description:
Whether or not US president fits the definition of a Russian asset, his actions align closely with the Kremlin’s interests
• Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Could Donald Trump be a Russian asset? The headline on a review in the Guardian of my new book Betrayal has provoked heated international debate. Written by the historian Lawrence Freedman, the piece generated thousands of comments from across Europe and beyond on social media. Many people responded with a single word: “Duh!”
Trump’s relationship with Vladimir Putin is the biggest mystery in international politics. In 2017 I wrote a book called Collusion, which set out Moscow’s operation to support and cultivate Trump, going back decades. The US president, of course, denies links with Russia. But in his second term, his behaviour towards Putin has been as weird and perplexing as during his first.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What’s really behind Trump’s deference to Putin?

articles.author: Margaret Sullivan
articles.description:
The president’s call for the FCC to scrutinize Kristen Welker’s innocuous remarks is a sign of desperation
With his approval ratings tanking, the crucial midterm elections looming, and his war with Iran turning into a quagmire, Donald Trump has entered full freak-out mode.
It’s not hard to tell. Just look at what happened this week when he lashed out at Kristen Welker, the well-respected host of NBC’s Meet the Press, and one of the best-known journalists in the nation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s threat against an NBC journalist is an attack on reality | Margaret Sullivan

articles.description:
The Canadian province's premier, Doug Ford, installed a billboard-sized sign on the lake's shoreline after the US president signed an executive order on Thursday directing US federal agencies to change the lake's name on US maps, documents and databases to 'Lake America'. Ford told reporters that the lake's name, which is more than 400 years old, would remain unchanged. Trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed last week, with each side ‌blaming the ⁠other for derailing three days of intensive negotiations


Trump signs executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

articles.title: Ontario premier unveils Lake Ontario sign in response to Trump’s ‘Lake America’ order – video

Jonathan Freedland speaks to Dan Alexander of Forbes about how Donald Trump made so much money last year at the same time trade wars, military wars and a rising national debt hurt the US economy

articles.description:
One of Donald Trump’s closest and most devoted aides, Natalie Harp, has faced intense media scrutiny this week, after a Democratic senator, Jon Ossoff, name-checked her in a speech that went viral. So what do we know about Harp, who is often referred to as the ‘human printer’? And why is everybody talking about her relationship with Trump? Helen Pidd speaks to international news editor Paul Owen

articles.title: Why is Trump’s ‘human printer’ aide Natalie Harp suddenly in the spotlight? - The Latest

articles.description:
Less than three months to go until the midterms, voters are thinking about grocery prices, the Iran war and… datacentres.

This week, Jonathan Freedland speaks to historian Jill Lepore about how this latest AI backlash could influence those all-important elections in November. Are we seeing the beginning of the end of the 'artificial state'?

articles.title: Historian Jill Lepore on the datacentre backlash | Politics Weekly America

articles.description:
Blaze causes electricity supply failure and disruption of services to airport and Reading
Hundreds of passengers were evacuated from a train, and services to Heathrow airport were cancelled, after a fire near tracks in the London Paddington area caused major disruptions to London’s rail network.
The fire caused an electricity supply failure which left all lines between Paddington and the airport blocked, National Rail said on Saturday afternoon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: London Paddington fire causes rail chaos as Heathrow trains cancelled

articles.author: Press Association
articles.description:
Duty falls by precedent to William to attend service of late monarch, alongside Princess Royal, who is godmother to new king Haakon VIII 
The Prince of Wales is to represent his father at the funeral of King Harald V of Norway next week, Buckingham Palace has announced.
William, the heir to the throne, will be joined by his aunt the Princess Royal, who is attending in a private and personal capacity as godmother of the new king, Haakon VIII.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prince William to represent King Charles at funeral of Norway’s King Harald V

articles.author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
articles.description:
Sector has avoided issue because of stigma fears, expert warns ahead of closure of Nottingham attacks inquiry 
Mental health organisations have “failed to acknowledge” the risk of violence from a minority of people with severe mental illnesses, the chief executive of Mind has said ahead of the closure of the inquiry into the Nottingham attacks.
Dr Sarah Hughes, who has led mental health charity Mind for four years and has worked in the sector for almost four decades, said charities had shied away from addressing the risk of violence due to the fact it had increased the stigma and harassment around people with mental health conditions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mental health groups have ‘failed to acknowledge’ risk of violence, says Mind chief

articles.author: Donna Ferguson, Priya Bharadia and agencies
articles.description:
Port authorities say access roads ‘free flowing’ again after large group forces road closures in both directions 
Dozens of people dressed in black and wearing balaclavas blocked the road at the port of Dover in Kent, forcing closures in both directions on Saturday morning.
Kent police said they were were in attendance and engaging with the protest, which the Port of Dover described as a “public order incident”. No arrests were made during the incident. Responsibility for the demonstration appears to have been claimed by an anti-immigration group with links to the far right.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Black-clad protesters in balaclavas block road at port of Dover in Kent

articles.author: Angus Thomson
articles.description:
Officers seize supercar in Southend after reports of it being driven at up to twice speed limit
Police have seized a Lamborghini potentially worth more than £200,000 under tightened laws introduced to crack down on dangerous driving.
Essex police confiscated the Lamborghini Huracan on Saturday afternoon after receiving reports of the supercar being driven dangerously in Southend. The car was travelling at speeds suspected to be more than twice the limit, police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police seize £200k Lamborghini under tightened antisocial driving laws

articles.author: Taz Ali (now) and Hamish Mackay (earlier)
articles.description:
‘Sometimes we will get things wrong and get a bit of a kicking for it,’ party leader tells gathering in Birmingham 
No real mention by Anderson of the problems that overshadowed events yesterday. He ended his opening speech saying: "Yesterday was great. Today is going to be absolutely brilliant.”
Laila Cunningham is speaking next.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Farage brushes aside Reform controversies in closing conference speech – UK politics as it happened

articles.author: Ben Quinn and Peter Walker
articles.description:
Reform UK leader maintains innocence in overseas funding controversy on last day of party conference
Nigel Farage has claimed that he “wasn’t even listening” during a meeting at the centre of a controversy about whether his party considered evading the law on accepting donations from overseas.
The Reform UK leader also claimed he knew donation law “better than anybody” during interviews as he sought to salvage the final day of his party conference from the fallout that has already cost him two of his closest aides.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I wasn’t even listening,’ Farage says of donations scandal meeting

articles.author: Ben Quinn
articles.description:
Ryan Bridge, arrested this year on suspicion of religiously and racially aggravated harassment, says party invited him
The leader of a flag campaign group who was arrested on suspicion of causing religiously and racially aggravated harassment was given access to Reform UK’s annual conference.
Ryan Bridge, whose Raise the Colours group has put up hundreds of union and St George flags across England, told the Guardian he was invited to the conference.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Raise the Colours leader given access to Reform UK conference while on bail

articles.author: Pippa Crerar, Heather Stewart and Jessica Elgot
articles.description:
MPs applaud PM’s ambition and optimism but John Healey has yet to show he can match leader’s radical perspective
Until now, Andy Burnham has been a lucky prime minister. In office for just over six weeks, no major domestic crisis derailed his plans over the summer, Reform has been on the back foot, and he arrived back at Westminster with his personal approval ratings soaring and optimism undampened.
But underneath the sense of relief that many Labour MPs are feeling that their high-stakes gamble of ousting Keir Starmer appears – for now – to have paid off, there is an unease that Burnham’s premiership is yet to make contact with economic reality.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The chancellor is in a bind’: is No 11 at odds with Burnham’s big vision?

articles.author: Amelia Hill
articles.description:
After bringing injured queen Phoebee home in July, Gilly McArthur expected her soon to die, but she’s bumbling on
Fifty-two days ago, Phoebee was lying by the side of a road in the blistering sun with a broken wing. Today, she’s clambering up the arm of Gilly McArthur, around the nape of her neck and disappearing into her hair.
“I couldn’t leave her by the roadside,” McArthur says. “So I bought her home and made her a bed of flowers. I thought she’d be dead in a day or so.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I could watch her for hours’: the woman who rescued a bee and created a buzz

articles.author: Donna Ferguson
articles.description:
As the government prepares to crack down on ‘phoney bargains’ we ask experts about what exactly constitutes a genuine price reduction
When is a sale not a sale? Online and on the high street, some shops just always seem to be selling at a discount.
Whether it’s the closing down sale that goes on for years, or the crossed-out original price that you can’t remember ever paying, some retailers try all kinds of ways to convince us we are getting a bargain.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Deal or no deal? How to know if the retail price is right

articles.author: Geraldine McKelvie
articles.description:
Chancellor says he wants to ensure country has ‘buffer’ against uncertainty as global bond yields hit 18-year high
The chancellor has indicated that the UK will face a tough budget next month due to Trump’s war in the Middle East.
In an interview with the Financial Times, John Healey said the conflict in Iran would probably have a strong influence on his first budget on 28 October.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: John Healey warns of tough first budget as Middle East war puts pressure on economy

articles.author: Chloe Mac Donnell
articles.description:
The ‘hip boost’ aims to create hourglass silhouette, much like Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand’s padded shorts
For decades shapewear has been used to compress and cinch. But now there is a sub-genre emerging. Rather than shrinking a silhouette, it aims to add inches.
This week M&S launched a bodysuit that features exaggerated padding at the hip allowing the wearer to create an hourglass shape, or at least the illusion of one.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kardashian curves: M&S launches £28 bodysuit with exaggerated hip padding

articles.author: Fiona Harvey in Birmingham
articles.description:
Climate scepticism is common at the Reform party conference, but many also criticise Labour for failing to protect Britons from hot weather
On the second day of the Reform UK conference, in the wake of an undercover investigation alleging party officials plotted to evade the law on foreign donations, the deputy leader, Richard Tice, addressed the audience. Within minutes, a banner appeared behind him reading: “Collect £5m, burn the planet.”
It was taken down promptly and Tice, who has repeatedly called on people to enjoy the summer’s five successive heatwaves and record drought, rolled on. As Reform members at the Birmingham venue applauded Tice, there was plenty of agreement with his views. “I enjoyed the heat this summer,” said Jeanette Bowden, of Bexley. “I don’t think people need telling to take care of themselves.” Her partner, James, added, without scientific backing: “Carbon dioxide was much higher in the past, it was 10 times higher than this during the ice ages. It’s not a human problem.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform continues to cast doubt on climate science. Do its supporters agree?

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Anwar, who lives in Glasgow, says Home Office refused visa application despite Maryam having cancer
A man living in the UK has said he believes his sister-in-law who died from cancer in Gaza would still be alive today if the Home Office had agreed to bring her and her family to Britain.
Anwar, who lives in Glasgow, fled Gaza in 2020 and was granted refugee status in the UK in 2021. After the destruction of large areas of Gaza by Israeli forces following the Hamas attacks on Israel in October 2023, he applied to bring his brother Hassan, Hassan’s wife, Maryam, their two young children and other family members to the UK in October 2025. He said the Home Office rejected their application.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gaza refugee says sister-in-law ‘would be alive’ if Home Office had let her come to UK

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Scale of deportations made public for first time amid criticism of hardline approach to UK citizens
Sweden has confirmed 458 British citizens have been deported or forcibly removed by police since Brexit.
It is the first time the scale of the deportations of citizens who failed to secure residency in Sweden post-Brexit has been made public and comes amid mounting criticism of a cruel and hardline approach to Britons who had chosen to make the country their home before Brexit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sweden confirms 458 Britons deported or forcibly removed since Brexit

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Six claims the party has faced – from an undisclosed £5m gift to an alleged plot to bypass election laws
As Reform UK’s annual conference unfolded in Birmingham, the party was once again facing heightened scrutiny over its finances.
Two senior officials have been suspended after they were filmed in an undercover investigation appearing to plot to get around electoral laws on foreign donations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The two-year trail of financial controversy dogging Reform and Farage

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Workers who blame algorithms for lowering their earnings are getting help from academics to find out how the system works
Gig economy workers are urging delivery platforms to open up the “black box” of computer-driven algorithms that determine the jobs they are offered and how much they are paid, blaming increased use of AI for lowering wages.
A group of food delivery riders in Edinburgh say their rates of pay have fallen and their working conditions have deteriorated at the same time as Deliveroo, Uber Eats and Just Eat, the three dominant gig economy platforms in the UK and Ireland, have increased their use of automation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Food delivery riders call on platforms to open up AI ‘black box’ they say has cut pay

articles.author: Natalie Wint
articles.description:
Experts say invasive species are creating ‘pollinator deserts’ and could have serious impact on food security
British beekeepers have called for a national awareness campaign about the impact of Asian hornets as they warned the invasive species was creating “pollinator deserts” and threatening food security.
Native to south-east Asia, the yellow-legged hornet is thought to have arrived in Europe in 2004 and has continued to spread ever since, its numbers probably boosted by increasingly warm springs and summers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Beekeepers warn of Asian hornet threat and call for UK awareness campaign

The Guardian journalist Michael Safi investigates a phenomenon labelled ‘AI psychosis’, travelling to the US to meet two people who have been on weird journeys with their chatbots
 Continue reading...

articles.title: 'Reform broke no law': Nigel Farage responds to latest donation revelations – video

articles.description:
Outlet faced significant financial challenges after it had funds blocked by bank without explanation
Workers at the leftwing news outlet the Canary fear it will not survive beyond this year amid access to funds being blocked and allegations of financial mismanagement and internal turmoil.
The site, which was founded in 2015 against a backdrop of the wave of support for the then Labour leader, Jeremy Corbyn, appeared set to expand after a multimillion-pound injection of funds last year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canary staff not paid amid fears for news website’s future

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspndent
articles.description:
With senior party figures appearing split and leader’s favourability rating dropping, questions about donations are causing yet more headaches

UK politics live – latest updates

Midway through an event at Reform’s annual conference on Friday there was question for the audience: who was worried about a Channel 4 News exposé of potential wrongdoing by party officials over donations? Almost no hands went up. The faithful might be sanguine. But make no mistake, Nigel Farage faces yet another problem.
Careful plans have been again upset. After months of answering – or primarily dodging – questions about his own finances, Farage had planned to use Reform UK’s biggest conference yet to make a blitz of policy announcements.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform UK exposé comes just as Farage was hoping to change the narrative

articles.description:
The potential breaches of the law exposed in an undercover film, what police say, and the party’s likely defence
Nigel Farage is facing yet another finance scandal following an undercover investigation into how Reform UK is funded. The potential wrongdoing – denied by the party – appears serious enough to have been immediately referred to the police by Labour and the Liberal Democrats. Here are the main legal issues for Reform and what any investigation will have to consider.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What is the latest finance scandal facing Reform UK?

articles.description:
CCTV footage shows a man jumping from a first-floor window before running into the street and, by chance. approaching a police car. The man jumps in and tells the officer he had been kidnapped and informs him of the location. Lincolnshire police subsequently arrest four men and a woman in connection with the incident
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man dives out of first-floor window to escape kidnappers in Lincolnshire - video

articles.description:
Nick Park began modelling the character as a feline, before finding it too difficult and changing him to a dog
The creator of Wallace and Gromit has revealed that the world’s most famous stop-motion animated dog was nearly a cat.
As Aardman Animations marks its 50th anniversary, Nick Park, who joined the studio in 1985, told the BBC he had originally modelled Gromit as a feline companion for Wallace.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wallace’s dog Gromit was nearly a cat, reveals creator as Aardman turns 50

articles.author: Daniella Lucas
articles.description:
As one card recently sold for £12m, opportunistic thefts have surged – envelopes are being opened en route, costing small businesses thousands
Pokémon’s success over the last 30 years has seen it grow from a much-loved Game Boy classic, to a world-dominating brand with TV shows, spin-off games, toys and even a theme park. The trading card game is a huge part of that, with more than 85bn cards printed over its lifetime, and the appetite for them shows no signs of slowing down. Packs get snapped up after release so quickly it’s now almost impossible to find them in shops, and a booming resale market is driving the hobby into murky waters.
One card recently sold for an eye-watering £12m, and an increasing number of people have gotten into the collecting business on the hunt for huge profits, leading to a rise in thefts targeting card shops. More recently though, some small businesses have reported that their sales have been hit by thieves targeting envelopes within Royal Mail, leading to thousands in lost revenue.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thieves target mail order sales as Pokémon card prices soar

By Alexis Okeowo. Read by Nneka Okoye

Support the Guardian today: theguardian.com/longreadpod

articles.author: Kiran Stacey and Damian Carrington
articles.description:
Exclusive: Angela Eagle urges UK citizens to be ‘a bit more resilient’ as they plan for national emergencies
British people have been urged to have enough food and water on hand to survive a few days without power or water, as the UN said the El Niño climate phenomenon was “supersizing before our eyes”, exacerbating extreme weather events worldwide.
Forecasters say they are braced for the biggest El Niño in 1,000 years, bringing wildfires and floods to parts of the world, and the threat of a wet, stormy winter for the UK.

 As the British government plans a campaign urging citizens to prepare for national emergencies, Angela Eagle told the Guardian the likelihood of a wild winter showed the importance of keeping supplies at home.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Minister tells Brits to stock up on days of supplies after ‘supersize’ El Niño warning

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield and Aisha Down
articles.description:

Now, a new stage musical is to give a nuanced and intimate portrait of that famous relationship, treat each as trailblazers in their own way and reveal parallels between the volatile state of the US during the 50s “red scare” and now.

It’s just the latest in a series of attempts from Trump’s administration to use video game memes and imagery to further its messaging.

Flappy Bill, perhaps the least gross, is a version of the old mobile hit Flappy Bird, except here you’re an eagle with a scroll in its claws. Supply Line could almost be an educational game about healthy food in schools, where you sort junk food off a conveyor belt destined for school lunches, except for some reason you play as a boxer who becomes more bloodied with every seed-oil containing, ultra-processed food item that you fail to punch into the garbage chute.

articles.description:
As FromSoftware’s new multiplayer game The Duskbloods nears release, the legendary game director behind Dark Souls talks connection, pessimism and of course, feet
Since 2009’s Demon’s Souls, Japanese video game director Hidetaka Miyazaki has shown the world a different way to think about game design. His games defy convention with punishing fights, obscure rules, and unknowable, inhospitable worlds. The “Soulslike” genre – named after Demon’s Souls and its sequel Dark Souls – is now ubiquitous, influencing multimillion-sellers from God of War and Star Wars: Jedi to Hollow Knight. Miyazaki’s most recent success, 2022’s Elden Ring, which credited Game of Thrones author George RR Martin as a co-creator, sold over 30m copies and inspired Alex Garland to adapt it for the big screen at A24. It earned Miyazaki a spot on Time magazine’s “most influential” list, an accolade he shares with just one other game developer: Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto.
Miyazaki is now 51 and has been FromSoftware’s president since 2014, elevated from game designer to CEO after the success of the Souls series. He has a cherubic face that could pass for 35. He rarely speaks publicly, and never on camera. When he does speak, he answers questions like one of his characters – softly, sadly, his head bowed, making eye-contact only when I am speaking. Outside the studio where we speak is the sprawl of Tokyo’s Shinjuku, an ever-changing maze where tourists get lost and pop-up stores appear and vanish without a trace. Today, a J-pop band performs in the square as the cicadas scream from the trees. A gilded statue of Malania, one of Elden Ring’s toughest bosses, looms over this dimly lit conference room inside From’s headquarters, a bonfire checkpoint away from the chaos.

articles.description:

The 30-minute preview scorched to No 1 on the viewing chart and even brought the site down for a few minutes as millions of gamers tried to watch what was, effectively, a very long teaser trailer. According to data collated by Eurogamer, more than 9,000 Twitch streamers covered the show leading to 5,227,798 hours of viewing there alone. And this was just the beginning of what will surely be two months of escalating hype – and unprecedented media attention.
Call me cynical, but I suspect the coverage of GTA VI in the media over the next few weeks will follow a familiar pattern. Mostly, it will be five-minute slots wedged in near the end of news bulletins in which games journalists, industry analysts and other pundits will be asked why the game is such a big deal, how much it cost to make and how much revenue it will generate. Perhaps a few will try to reignite the hoary old “violence in video games” debate, there will be presenters laughingly admitting they’ve not touched a game since Pac-Man, rolling their eyes and wallowing in their ignorance, in a way they never would while discussing any other art form. Somebody will venture the subversive view that “games are no longer just for kids”; somebody else will say “games make more money than films and music put together”. And that will be that, job done for another decade … or until there’s a funny story about Pokémon.
 Continue reading...

Perhaps you’ve led a scheming dynasty in Crusader Kings, or watched a favourite hero succumb to madness in Darkest Dungeon. Maybe you’ve surrendered yourself to the infinite yarn-spinner that is Dwarf Fortress – or read about it from the mid-00s forums where users helped popularise the term “Let’s Play” by chronicling their games in descriptive posts. Or perhaps you’ve played Firaxis’ XCOM, the alien invasion tactics hit that several key members of Zero Company studio Bit Reactor had a hand in.
Zero Company hinges on a concept as simple as it is perfect: take the complementary class abilities, tough dice rolls, and permanent character deaths of XCOM, and house them in a sci-fi setting known for spaghetti western blaster duels, last stands and heroic sacrifices. As creative director Greg Foertsch puts it, “Star Wars is about loss.” Which losses you end up mourning in Zero Company depends on you.
